data.body:
Phase 1 classification — MECHANISM CONFIRMED; DEFECT LEGITIMACY CANNOT-DETERMINE

Confirmed mechanism: commit d9e0f0e733 replaced the self-contained git subprocesses in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_concurrency.py` with `from rebar_reconciler import git_adapter` at line 55. A fresh process that directly execs the private file under a flat key with `find_spec("rebar_reconciler") is None` reaches that line and deterministically raises `ModuleNotFoundError`; executing the pre-d9 source under the identical package-free loader returns the real temporary repository HEAD. This proves the raw direct-file behavior changed at d9.

Discriminating evidence against a production defect: the sole production loader/caller is `applier._load_concurrency()` (`applier.py:268-277`, called at :587), but `applier.py` itself requires package context at module import starting at line 65. The supported in-process loader explicitly registers a real `rebar_reconciler` package before importing applier (`src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:174-186`), and the supported subprocess launcher prepends the engine directory so that package resolves (`src/rebar/_engine.py:75-100`). Fresh-process runtime probes through both supported shapes loaded `_concurrency`, returned the real git HEAD, and showed the package registered before `_concurrency.py` executed. A full production caller census found no second loader. The canonical-identity probe observed calls through the pre-seeded `rebar_reconciler.git_adapter` spy and found exactly one sys.modules object for `git_adapter.py`, rejecting an identity split. Existing concurrency tests pass 7/7 because the unit conftest deliberately supplies the package bridge.

Legitimacy is fail-closed `cannot-determine`, not yet `defect`: `_concurrency.py:1-6` is private and says it is inert on its own; ADR 0083:28-48 calls it location-pinned but does not promise context-free execution. `_loader.py:1-29` says several modules support standalone execution without naming every location-pinned module. Unlike the confirmed parent bug, `_concurrency.py` has no explicit standalone bootstrap contract and no user-visible failing supported entry point. Conversely, d9 explicitly claimed “Behaviour unchanged,” and package-free direct execution did work before it.

Decision required before Phase 2: must every location-pinned/by-file-loaded reconciler module execute without package context, or only modules with an explicit standalone bootstrap contract? Choosing the former makes this a defect and authorizes the proposed canonical lazy-load repair; choosing the latter makes the report a misunderstanding/unsupported private invocation and the ticket should close without code. Per rebar-debug, no test or repair is being added until that intended-behavior target is decided.
